{
  "action": "update_existing",
  "question_ids": ["v1", "v3"],
  "same_claim_as": ["e3", "e8", "e9", "e26", "e29"],
  "revises": ["e29"],
  "opposes": [],
  "independent_sources": false,
  "original_source": "Sharon AI, in its 8-K filing dated 2026-06-12; Tom's Hardware reported the disclosure on 2026-07-02.",
  "new_information": "Sharon AI’s filing provides primary-source detail that its agreement covers six years and 72 MW of new Australian data-center capacity built to Nvidia’s DSX AI factory design, with capacity scaling to as many as 40,000 Grace Blackwell GB300 GPUs. This gives scale, duration, and a formal company disclosure for Sharon AI’s participation previously reported by other sources. It does not disclose Nvidia’s financial commitment, a guarantee amount, the revenue-share percentage, or whether Nvidia must rent back or purchase unused capacity. The 72 MW and six-year term describe the agreement and facility, not a quantified Nvidia obligation for the FY2027 filing.",
  "arguments": [
    {
      "question_id": "v1",
      "statement": "The best-supported current estimate remains rung 2: NVIDIA’s disclosed FY2027 amount for guarantees and similar obligations is not established, while the quantified evidence cited so far points to a scale near $10 billion. The CoreWeave capacity-purchase commitment of $6.3 billion and the additional $3.5 billion for customer data-center lease guarantees are the strongest quantified evidence (e12, fact reported second-hand; e13, filing-based fact reported second-hand). Sharon AI’s 8-K adds evidence of a six-year, 72 MW arrangement scaling to as many as 40,000 GB300 GPUs, making the associated cloud program more concrete, but it does not state an NVIDIA guarantee or other financial obligation amount and does not justify moving the FY2027 estimate to another rung.",
      "support_ids": ["e1", "e4", "e12", "e13", "incoming"],
      "opposing_ids": [],
      "limitations": [
        "The $6.3 billion and $3.5 billion figures are not an aggregate FY2027 filing amount; the records describe different commitments and periods.",
        "The incoming primary-source disclosure quantifies facility capacity and agreement duration, not NVIDIA’s financial exposure.",
        "The broader guarantee report in e1 is a rumour; the program announcement in e4 does not quantify commitments.",
        "The filing amount in question is not yet established."
      ],
      "what_would_change_it": [
        "NVIDIA’s FY2027 annual filing, especially its disclosed aggregate amount and definitions for guarantees and similar obligations.",
        "A filing or contract disclosure specifying whether the Sharon AI agreement creates an NVIDIA guarantee or other financial commitment and quantifying it."
      ]
    },
    {
      "question_id": "v3",
      "statement": "The FY2027 reported amount for AI-cloud customer backstop arrangements remains unestablished, so no rung is confirmed. The current evidence indicates potentially material exposure: reports describe the backstop model and possible rent-back of unused GPUs (e27–e28, reporting), NVIDIA describes the revenue-sharing and credit-support model (e30, party statement), and DatacenterDynamics reports a $6.3 billion initial CoreWeave agreement value and a $1.5 billion Lambda deal value (e33–e34, reporting). Sharon AI’s 8-K now provides primary-source evidence of a six-year, 72 MW agreement scaling to as many as 40,000 GB300 GPUs, revising the earlier report that Sharon had adopted the offer (e29). However, the filing does not quantify any NVIDIA backstop or financing obligation, so it cannot establish that the FY2027 reported commitments meet any particular rung threshold.",
      "support_ids": ["e27", "e28", "e29", "e30", "e33", "e34", "incoming"],
      "opposing_ids": [],
      "limitations": [
        "The incoming filing identifies agreement duration and facility/GPU capacity, not the amount or legal form of any NVIDIA financing or backstop commitment.",
        "The reported CoreWeave and Lambda values are not established as amounts that NVIDIA will report under this question’s definition or at the FY2027 filing date.",
        "The reported rent-back mechanism and agreement values are third-party reporting; e29 was a report of adoption, now supported by the Sharon AI filing, but the filing details supplied here do not specify the backstop terms.",
        "The records do not provide the aggregate FY2027 reported commitment amount."
      ],
      "what_would_change_it": [
        "NVIDIA’s FY2027 annual filing disclosing the aggregate amount and scope of AI-cloud customer backstop commitments.",
        "A Sharon AI or NVIDIA filing, contract, or other primary disclosure specifying the financial-support terms and any amount attributable to this agreement."
      ]
    }
  ],
  "new_question": "",
  "independent_judgement": "",
  "reason": "The filing adds primary-source detail about the scale and duration of a named partner agreement and strengthens the evidence that Sharon AI adopted the program. That moves the context and risk assessment for existing questions about NVIDIA’s cloud-provider obligations and AI-cloud backstops, but does not quantify NVIDIA’s exposure or establish an FY2027 filing amount. The same-claim set includes prior reports of Sharon AI’s participation and up-to-40,000-GPU deployment; the Sharon AI disclosure is not independent of e26, which also attributes the GPU deployment claim to Sharon AI."
}

answer.original_source: Sharon AI, in its 8-K filing dated 2026-06-12; Tom's Hardware reported the disclosure on 2026-07-02.
answer.new_information: Sharon AI’s filing provides primary-source detail that its agreement covers six years and 72 MW of new Australian data-center capacity built to Nvidia’s DSX AI factory design, with capacity scaling to as many as 40,000 Grace Blackwell GB300 GPUs. This gives scale, duration, and a formal company disclosure for Sharon AI’s participation previously reported by other sources. It does not disclose Nvidia’s financial commitment, a guarantee amount, the revenue-share percentage, or whether Nvidia must rent back or purchase unused capacity. The 72 MW and six-year term describe the agreement and facility, not a quantified Nvidia obligation for the FY2027 filing.

arguments.statement: The best-supported current estimate remains rung 2: NVIDIA’s disclosed FY2027 amount for guarantees and similar obligations is not established, while the quantified evidence cited so far points to a scale near $10 billion. The CoreWeave capacity-purchase commitment of $6.3 billion and the additional $3.5 billion for customer data-center lease guarantees are the strongest quantified evidence (e12, fact reported second-hand; e13, filing-based fact reported second-hand). Sharon AI’s 8-K adds evidence of a six-year, 72 MW arrangement scaling to as many as 40,000 GB300 GPUs, making the associated cloud program more concrete, but it does not state an NVIDIA guarantee or other financial obligation amount and does not justify moving the FY2027 estimate to another rung.
limitations: The $6.3 billion and $3.5 billion figures are not an aggregate FY2027 filing amount; the records describe different commitments and periods.
The incoming primary-source disclosure quantifies facility capacity and agreement duration, not NVIDIA’s financial exposure.
The broader guarantee report in e1 is a rumour; the program announcement in e4 does not quantify commitments.
The filing amount in question is not yet established.
what_would_change_it: NVIDIA’s FY2027 annual filing, especially its disclosed aggregate amount and definitions for guarantees and similar obligations.
A filing or contract disclosure specifying whether the Sharon AI agreement creates an NVIDIA guarantee or other financial commitment and quantifying it.

arguments.statement: The FY2027 reported amount for AI-cloud customer backstop arrangements remains unestablished, so no rung is confirmed. The current evidence indicates potentially material exposure: reports describe the backstop model and possible rent-back of unused GPUs (e27–e28, reporting), NVIDIA describes the revenue-sharing and credit-support model (e30, party statement), and DatacenterDynamics reports a $6.3 billion initial CoreWeave agreement value and a $1.5 billion Lambda deal value (e33–e34, reporting). Sharon AI’s 8-K now provides primary-source evidence of a six-year, 72 MW agreement scaling to as many as 40,000 GB300 GPUs, revising the earlier report that Sharon had adopted the offer (e29). However, the filing does not quantify any NVIDIA backstop or financing obligation, so it cannot establish that the FY2027 reported commitments meet any particular rung threshold.
limitations: The incoming filing identifies agreement duration and facility/GPU capacity, not the amount or legal form of any NVIDIA financing or backstop commitment.
The reported CoreWeave and Lambda values are not established as amounts that NVIDIA will report under this question’s definition or at the FY2027 filing date.

The reported rent-back mechanism and agreement values are third-party reporting; e29 was a report of adoption, now supported by the Sharon AI filing, but the filing details supplied here do not specify the backstop terms.
The records do not provide the aggregate FY2027 reported commitment amount.
what_would_change_it: NVIDIA’s FY2027 annual filing disclosing the aggregate amount and scope of AI-cloud customer backstop commitments.
A Sharon AI or NVIDIA filing, contract, or other primary disclosure specifying the financial-support terms and any amount attributable to this agreement.

answer.reason: The filing adds primary-source detail about the scale and duration of a named partner agreement and strengthens the evidence that Sharon AI adopted the program. That moves the context and risk assessment for existing questions about NVIDIA’s cloud-provider obligations and AI-cloud backstops, but does not quantify NVIDIA’s exposure or establish an FY2027 filing amount. The same-claim set includes prior reports of Sharon AI’s participation and up-to-40,000-GPU deployment; the Sharon AI disclosure is not independent of e26, which also attributes the GPU deployment claim to Sharon AI.
